AcarsMessage.description:
One ACARS block (: MSK 2400 bit/s over AM, ARINC 618 framing). Field names follow
the standard's, so a message here reads the same as in every other ACARS tool.

ack.description: Technical acknowledgement: the block being acknowledged, or `None` for a NAK.

block_id.description: Block identifier. `0`–`9` marks a downlink (aircraft to ground).

label.description: Two-character label identifying the message type (`5Z`, `H1`, `_d` …).

mode.description: Mode character — `2` is VHF category A.

more.description: The block ended with ETB rather than ETX: another block of the same message follows.

registration.description: Aircraft registration with the standard `.` padding removed.

seq_no.description: Message sequence number, on downlinks only.

AdsbMessage.description:
One decoded Mode S / ADS-B frame (: preamble correlation + Mode S CRC).
Fields are `Option` because which ones a frame carries depends on its type code — a
position frame has no callsign, an identification frame has no altitude.

df.description: Downlink Format (17 = ADS-B extended squitter, 11 = all-call reply).

icao.description: ICAO 24-bit address as 6 hex digits — the aircraft's identity across frames.

lat.description: Latitude in degrees, once a CPR even/odd pair has been solved.

raw.description: The raw frame as hex — the interop format every Mode S tool speaks.

type_code.description: Extended-squitter type code, when the frame has an ME field.

crc_fix.description:
Repair single-bit errors the Mode S CRC localizes. Off trades sensitivity for a
lower false-frame rate on a noisy antenna.

ref_lat.description:
Reference position for locally-decoded (single-frame) CPR positions, in degrees.
Without one, a position needs a matching even/odd frame pair.

AisChannel.description:
Which of the two AIS channels a receiver is parked on. Only the label travels with the
decoded message — the tuning itself is the channel's `offset_hz`.

AisMessage.description: One decoded AIS message (: GMSK/NRZI over HDLC framing).

ais_channel.description: Which of the two AIS channels the burst arrived on (`A` = 161.975 MHz).

mmsi.description: Maritime Mobile Service Identity — the vessel's identity across messages.

msg_type.description: ITU-R M.1371 message type (1–3 position report, 5 static data, 18/19 class B …).

nav_status.description: Navigational status code (0 = under way using engine …).

nmea.description: The `!AIVDM` sentence — the interop format every AIS tool speaks.

AntennaDesign.description:
The antenna to cut. Adjacently tagged like [`crate::ChannelParams`]: the designs that take
no choices are bare tags, the rest carry their settings.

AntennaGeometry.description: The antenna as a shape: enough to draw it to scale from any angle.

AntennaPart.description: One thing to cut, bend or buy.

count.description: How many of this part the design needs.

position_m.description:
Where it sits along the boom, measured from the reflector. Only the designs that have
a boom set it.

AntennaPoint.description:
A point on the antenna, in metres from the origin. `x` runs along the elements, `y` is up,
`z` is the boom's depth. The origin is the feedpoint, or the base of anything that stands on
one.

balanced.description: Whether the feedpoint is balanced, and so wants a balun ahead of coax.

design.description: The design that produced this, echoed so a cached report can name itself.

feedpoint_ohms.description:
Estimated feedpoint impedance in free space. `None` where the design's own matching
network sets it and a raw figure would mislead.

geometry.description: The same design as a shape, to scale, for a drawing of it.

notes.description:
Everything the numbers alone do not say: what to trim, what to match with, what the
estimate assumes.

wavelength_m.description: Free-space wavelength, before any correction factor.

feedline_velocity_factor.description:
Velocity factor of the coax, used only by designs that include a matching section.
Solid polyethylene is 0.66, foam 0.80, PTFE 0.70.

velocity_factor.description: End-effect factor applied to every resonant element.

AntennaSegment.description: One straight piece of the antenna, as drawn.

label.description:
The part this piece is. Where the report lists a part under the same name, the segment is
exactly that long.

AntennaSegmentRole.description: What a drawn piece does, so a view can colour it without reading its name.

ApiError.description: Uniform error body for REST failures.

ApplyTemplateRequest.description: Apply a built-in template to a live device set.

AprsPacket.description:
One decoded AX.25 frame, with the APRS fields parsed out when the info field carries them
(: AFSK1200 + 9600 G3RUH).

mic_e_message.description:
The Mic-E message the operator selected, named (APRS 1.0.1 ch. 10): one of the 7
standard messages, one of the 7 custom ones, or `Emergency`. `Unknown` is the spec's
own word for a packet whose three message bits mix the standard and custom tables.
Absent on every packet that is not Mic-E.

symbol.description: APRS symbol as `table` + `code`, e.g. `/>` for a car.

tnc2.description: TNC2 monitor line (`SRC>DEST,PATH:info`) — the interop format.

ArgumentOption.description: One labelled value in a driver's discrete option list.

ArgumentType.description:
The exact type SoapySDR declares for an argument. This stays separate from
[`ExtraSetting`], which is the compact control shape used by the existing receiver UI.

Attribution.description: One third-party component the release distributes.

license.description:
The SPDX expression the component declares for itself, verbatim. Not normalized:
`MIT/Apache-2.0` and `MIT OR Apache-2.0` are the same offer, but only one of them is
what the package actually says, and the notice should say what the package says.

note.description:
Set only where the SPDX id is not the whole story: a copyleft relink offer, a patent
encumbrance, a library that is loaded but never linked.

texts.description:
Ids of the license texts this component ships, resolvable through
`GET /api/about/licenses/{id}`. Empty when the component declares an SPDX expression but
publishes no license file of its own — common for crates that rely on the SPDX id alone.

Always serialized, empty included: a client that has to tell "no texts" apart from "the
field was omitted" is a client that will one day render neither.

version.description: Absent for native libraries, whose version is whatever the platform package pinned.

AtvColor.description:
Colour encoding carried on the composite-video subcarrier. Monochrome leaves the
subcarrier untouched and works at the lower sample rates used by narrow-band ATV.

AtvModulation.description:
How an analog television transmission carries its video, and with it the polarity the
demodulated signal arrives in (: ATV).

bandwidth_hz.description:
Video channel width in Hz. This *is* the horizontal resolution — a picture cannot carry
more detail per line than the bandwidth that delivered it — so it is the one knob worth
opening up when the channel is clean, bounded by the mode's IQ rate.

color.description:
Composite colour system. PAL and NTSC need a device rate wide enough to contain their
4.43 MHz or 3.58 MHz subcarrier respectively.

interlace.description:
Weave the two fields into one frame at their real line positions. Off decodes each
vertical sync as a whole progressive frame, which is what non-interlaced amateur and
camera sources send.

invert.description:
Invert the video polarity, for a transmission that keys the opposite way round from its
modulation's convention (see [`AtvModulation`]). A picture that comes out as a photographic
negative, with the sync tracker never locking, is what this fixes.

sound_subcarrier_hz.description:
FM sound carrier above the picture carrier, in Hz. Common values are 4.5, 5.5, 6.0 and
6.5 MHz. `None` keeps ATV usable on receivers that only cover the luma channel.

AtvStandard.description:
Scanning standard the transmission follows: how many lines make a frame and how fast they
go by. Everything else the demodulator needs — porch widths, active window, blanked lines —
derives from these two numbers plus the standard's own timings.

AudioAgcMode.description:
How hard the audio AGC rides the level. The speeds are the ones a radio's own switch offers,
because they are the ones that suit the modes: slow for SSB speech, fast for a band being
tuned across, medium for everything else.

AudioFilterSettings.description:
Adjustable audio passband — the "narrow the filter until only the voice is left" control,
after demodulation rather than in the RF channel.

high_hz.description: High cut. Hiss and splatter live above it.

low_hz.description: Low cut. Rumble, hum and the subaudible band live below this.

AudioProcessing.description:
Everything a voice channel does to its audio after the demodulator, plus the one stage that
has to run before it.

Stages run in the order they are declared: the blanker on IQ, then passband, notches,
adaptive notch, noise reduction and AGC on the demodulated audio. Filtering first keeps the
junk outside the passband out of everything downstream, and the AGC runs last so what it
levels is what the listener actually hears.

Every stage is off by default, which is what a channel had before this existed.

auto_notch.description: Remove steady carriers without being told where they are.

AuthInfo.description:
`GET /api/auth` — unauthenticated, so a client knows whether to ask for a token before
its first real request (: optional single shared token).

token_required.description: Whether this server rejects requests without the shared token.

BandAllocation.description: What a stretch of spectrum is allocated to, as one layer states it.

aliases.description:
Other names the explorer matches on — wavelengths ("70 cm"), colloquialisms ("CB"),
and the service spelled the long way ("marine", "maritime mobile").

channel_step_hz.description: Channel raster, where the band is channelized.

name.description:
What an operator calls it: "2 m amateur", "Marine VHF", "Airband". From the annotations
overlay where one applies, otherwise the same as [`Self::official_name`].

official_name.description:
Exactly what the source document calls it — "MOBILER SEEFUNKDIENST", "MARITIME MOBILE".
Kept beside the friendly name rather than replaced by it: the regulator's wording is the
citable one, and it is what a reader checking against the source will search for.

primary.description:
Primary allocation rather than secondary. Both the ITU and BNetzA tables carry this as
capitalisation — `MARITIME MOBILE` is primary, `Maritime mobile` is secondary — and a
secondary service must accept interference from every primary one, which is the
difference between "this band is yours" and "you may use it if nobody else is".

reference.description:
Where the row came from inside its source document: `Eintrag 27001`, `FREQ_00001`,
a page number. `None` for the curated layers, which are their own provenance.

oneOf.description:
The mode to tune with, where the band has an obvious one. Sent to the channel verbatim,
so "tune here with the suggested mode" needs no client-side mode table.

covered.description:
Everything else covering it, most specific first — co-allocations from the winner's own
layer, then the layers underneath. This is what lets the identify popover say "BNetzA
calls it X, over ITU's Y", and what keeps a co-primary service from vanishing.

BandLane.description:
A row of the ruler. The regulatory layers merge into one lane by most-specific-wins; an
overlay is a lane of its own, because it describes the same spectrum from a different angle
rather than contradicting it.

blocks.description:
Sorted by `start_hz`, non-overlapping — the resolution is what removes the overlaps the
source tables are full of.

overlay.description: Whether the lane is supplementary and may be switched off without losing the allocation.

BandLayerInfo.description:
One source of allocations: a table someone published, identified so a block can say where it
came from. Adding a region is adding one of these plus its entries ('s "pluggable
importers"); nothing else in the resolution knows the difference.

rank.description:
Least-specific first: where this layer sits when two of them cover one frequency. Ties
cannot happen — every layer in a region has a distinct rank.

source.description:
The document and edition the entries were taken from, so a stale table is visible rather
than merely wrong.

allocations.description:
Every allocation the lanes reference, once. [`BandBlock::of`] and [`BandBlock::covered`]
index into this; it is also what the explorer searches, which is why search needs no
deduplication of its own.

layers.description: Every layer the lanes reference, so a block's `layer` id resolves without a second call.

BandRegion.description: A region the operator can select: the ITU region plus whichever regulator applies there.

country.description:
ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 where the region is one country; `None` for the bare ITU regions and
for CEPT.

approximate.description:
True when only the ITU region could be decided — the coordinate is outside every
national footprint this build ships, so the answer is coarse and the UI should say so.

region.description:
The most specific region whose footprint contains the coordinate; never empty, because
the three ITU regions cover the globe.

default_region.description: What a client with no stored preference should select.

BandService.description:
The service category a block belongs to. Drives the ruler's colour, so it is deliberately
coarse: ten categories a reader can hold in their head, not the ITU's full service list.

mode.description: Suggested channel type id (e.g. `"nfm"`), if any.

BroadcastStatus.description:
Periodic acquisition report from a wideband digital-broadcast channel. These values describe
the RF lock itself; absent service fields mean the multiplex has not been decoded.

BroadcastSystem.description: Broadcast waveform identified by a standards-specific synchronizer.

oneOf.description:
Full per-direction, per-channel capability data. Older backends and stored payloads omit
it; Soapy-backed devices always populate it.

duplex.description:
Which directions this radio has, and whether it can run them together. Receive-only
unless a backend says otherwise, so a device cannot advertise a transmitter by omission.
This is the *hardware's* shape, not a permission: transmit stays behind an
authorized-use switch that does not exist, so a `half` radio still transmits nothing.

freq_ranges.description: Tunable center-frequency ranges in Hz (multiple = discontiguous tuner ranges).

per_stream.description:
Which settings each receive stream holds on its own. Which settings are per-stream is a
property of the *radio* — a coherent array shares one tuning by definition while a
two-daughterboard USRP genuinely has two — so the radio declares it, the same way it
declares gains and antennas.

ppm.description:
Whether the radio has a frequency-correction setting at all. Several do not — HackRF has
no correction register, SpyServer's protocol carries no such field, a Soapy tuner without
a `CORR` component cannot apply one — and their backends already refuse `ppm` outright,
while a recording and the signal generator swallow it and do nothing. Without this the
client drew the control on every device, so a knob that could only error, or only lie,
looked exactly like one that worked.

Defaults to *unsupported* for the same reason `duplex` defaults to receive-only: a
capability must be declared, never advertised by omission.

rx_streams.description:
How many independent receive streams this radio delivers at once. One for an ordinary
SDR; a KrakenSDR is five coherent channels on one USB device, which is why this is a
count and not a bool. A device node draws one IQ output per stream.

sample_rates.description: Supported sample rates in samples/s. Empty means "continuous", use `sample_rate_range`.

tx_streams.description:
How many independent transmit streams it accepts. Reported for symmetry and for the
device picker; the canvas still draws a single reserved transmit input, because there is
nothing to wire into it until transmit lands.

ChannelCapabilities.description: Capabilities of one hardware channel in one signal direction.

bandwidth_hz.description: Nominal RF bandwidth the channel needs, in Hz.

decoder_kind.description:
[`crate::DecoderEvent::kind`] this channel emits, when it is a decoder — the client
uses it to pick the panel that renders the events.

has_audio.description:
Whether the channel produces listenable audio. Data decoders ( wave 1) do
not, so the client hides their audio controls instead of offering a silent stream.
Defaults to `true` so a snapshot from an older peer keeps the pre-M4 behaviour.

has_video.description:
Whether the channel produces a picture, delivered as [`crate::VideoFrame`] binary frames
rather than as decoder events (ATV). The client subscribes and mounts a video
panel on the channel's face when this is set. Defaults to `false`, which is every mode
that predates the video transport.

input_rate_hz.description: IQ rate the demod expects from the DDC, in Hz.

native_rate_max_hz.description:
Set when the channel is handed the device's **own** samples — mixed to its offset, never
resampled. `input_rate_hz` is then the lowest device rate it can run at and this the
highest, so a receiver is set anywhere in that range rather than to one exact number.

ADS-B preserves pulse timing, ATV retains wide chroma and sound subcarriers, and GNSS
retains chip timing. Mutually exclusive with `exact_rate_only`.

needs_position.description: Whether this channel accepts a live station position input.

ChannelInfo.description: A live channel instance inside a device set.

stream.description:
Which of the device's receive streams feeds this channel. Defaults to 0 because a peer
that predates multi-stream devices names no stream and means the only one its radio has.

ChannelLevel.description:
One channel's live signal level.

Its own message rather than a field of [`crate::ChannelInfo`]: a level changes continuously,
and carrying it in the state snapshot would make every reading a state invalidation. Levels
are dBFS of the channel's filtered passband, where unit-magnitude IQ is 0 dBFS — the same
scale the squelch threshold is set on, so the two are directly comparable.

level_db.description: Smoothed level: fast to rise, slow to fall.

peak_db.description: Loudest recent level, held then decayed.

ChannelNode.description:
A channel node's payload. The *type* is topology — it decides the node's ports — while the
settings behind it stay on the engine's channel (module docs).

ChannelParams.description:
Type-discriminated demod parameters. Adjacently tagged so the generated TS is a
discriminated union on `type`, and `{"type":"nfm","settings":{}}` deserializes with
every field at its default.

ChannelSettings.description: Per-channel settings: where the channel sits and how it demodulates.

audio.description:
Blanker, filters, noise reduction and AGC. Shared by every voice mode rather than
written into each one's params, so what an operator learns on one channel is the same
control on the next.

offset_hz.description: Offset from the device center frequency, in Hz.

squelch_db.description:
Squelch threshold in dBFS, measured on the channel-filtered IQ (the mode's occupied
bandwidth, not the full DDC passband); `None` = squelch open.

CheckStatus.description:
How a check came out. `Warn` is "works, but something is degraded or absent"; `Fail` is
"this will not work as configured".

fps.description: Requested frame rate; server clamps to its supported range.

stream.description:
Which receive stream's spectrum. Defaults to 0 so a client that predates
multi-stream devices keeps its subscription; which stream a binary frame carries is
implicit in this subscription, never a frame header field.

Stop one receive stream's spectrum. `stream` defaults to 0, so a client that predates

would silence every other lane of the same radio on this connection.

Stop one receive stream's spectrum. `stream` defaults to 0, so a client that predates

would silence every other lane of the same radio on this connection.

the channel's own rate; answered with `IqStreamStarted`.

The burst size and cadence are the server's, not the client's: they are what bounds the

a device-position node in the active workspace.

`GET /api/clients` — how many clients share this server right now ( M5
multi-client). Includes the caller.

ComponentSource.description:
Which part of the product a component arrives through.

The distinction is about how it reaches the user, not about language: [`Native`] components
are shipped as libraries next to the binary and loaded at runtime, so their obligations
attach to the installer rather than to the executable.

[`Native`]: ComponentSource::Native

CreateChannelRequest.description: `POST /api/devicesets/{ds}/channels` — add a channel to a device set.

stream.description:
Which of the device's receive streams the channel taps. Defaults to 0 so a client that
predates multi-stream devices keeps meaning the only stream its radio has; out of range
is a bad request naming the count, never a silent fallback.

CreateDeviceSetRequest.description: `POST /api/devicesets` — open a device into a new device set.

CreatePresetRequest.description: `POST /api/presets` — snapshot the active workspace's radios under a name.

Workspace to start from; omitted means [`WorkspaceSnapshot::empty`] — a new workspace is a
clean bench. Only the first workspace a fresh install seeds opens on a starter workspace.

CreatedRowId.description: Identifier returned when a persistence row (preset, bookmark) is created.

DabMode.description:
DAB generations share the same EN 300 401 Mode I RF waveform. `Auto` reports the ensemble
without assuming which audio component type its FIC will eventually announce.

symbol_rate.description:
Symbol rate in baud. The channel rate supports narrow-band amateur television carriers
through 1 MBd; wider transponders need a receiver stream wider than this channel type.

freq_hz.description: Absolute RF frequency of the channel when the frame arrived, in Hz.

station.description: Emitter identity within the decoder (ICAO, MMSI, callsign, pager address).

DecoderLogResponse.description: `GET /api/decoderlog` — newest first, bounded by the requested `limit`.

dropped.description:
Frames dropped on the way to the log since the server started, because a consumer
fell behind (: bounded queues surface their loss).

DeletedCount.description: `DELETE /api/decoderlog` — how many rows the filtered clear removed.

strength.description:
How much of the tracked noise floor is subtracted, `0.0..=1.0`. Past the middle of the
range the residue starts to sound processed, which is a taste, not a fault.

driver.description: Driver id that produced this entry: `"virtual"`, `"soapy"`, `"rtlsdr"`, …

key.description: Stable per-device key within a driver (serial, index, or file path).

label.description: Human label for the device picker.

oneOf.description:
What the driver can say about this radio *without opening it* — enough to tell whether a
workspace template could run here, so the picker offers only the devices that fit.

`None` means "not known until it is opened", which is what a backend that has to ask the
hardware reports (Soapy). Unknown is never read as capable: a device with no profile is
offered with that said plainly, rather than filtered in on a guess.

It is deliberately narrower than [`Capabilities`]: everything here is a fact about the
*model*, so a driver can answer from a table. Gain stages, antennas and the extras are
the unit's and are read when it opens — reporting an empty gain list at probe time would
not read as "not asked yet", it would read as "no gain control".

serial.description: Serial number when the driver exposes one (used to collapse probe duplicates).

DeviceProfile.description:
The part of a radio's capability that is a property of the model rather than the unit.

Split out so it can be answered twice from one declaration: by a probe, which has only a USB
descriptor, and by [`Capabilities::profile`] on a radio that is already open. Nothing
constructs it by hand — it is always a projection of a full capability set, which is what
keeps the two from drifting.

freq_ranges.description: Tunable centre-frequency ranges in Hz (multiple = discontiguous tuner ranges).

per_stream.description:
Which settings each stream holds on its own — a property of the model, so the picker can
tell a coherent array from a bank of independent tuners without opening the radio.

sample_rates.description: Supported sample rates in samples/s. Empty means "continuous", use `sample_rate_range`.

key.description: Per-driver key, used without a serial or to distinguish variants sharing one serial.

DeviceSet.description: One opened device and everything hosted on it (: "one device set per opened device").

oneOf.description: Active raw-IQ network export, if any.

overruns.description:
Cumulative device samples dropped at the capture ring since the set opened. Growth
means the DSP thread cannot keep up — audio and spectrum have gaps even while
`status` stays `running` ( backpressure; CLAUDE.md no-silent-failure).

oneOf.description: Replay transport, on a set whose device is a recording rather than a radio.
Active IQ recording, if any.

Running frequency scan, if any. While a scan runs the set's
`settings.center_hz` moves every dwell, so live progress arrives as
[`crate::ServerEvent::ScannerUpdate`] rather than one `StateChanged` per step.

DeviceSetStatus.description: Runtime status of a device set's capture.

DeviceSettings.description: A mutation applied to a device. Absent fields are left unchanged ( PATCH device).

bandwidth.description: Hardware baseband filter bandwidth in Hz.

streams.description:
Per-stream overrides, by stream index. Only the fields [`Capabilities::per_stream`] marks
as per-stream are read here; the rest are the radio's and live above.

DirectionalCapabilities.description:
Directional and runtime capabilities that cannot be represented by the legacy channel-0
receiver fields on [`Capabilities`].

DmrSlots.description:
Which DMR timeslot a channel reports and plays. Both slots share one 12.5 kHz carrier in
30 ms alternation, so the receiver always hears both; this decides what reaches its outputs.

hint.description: What to do about it, when there is something to do.

bandwidth_hz.description:
Occupied bandwidth in Hz. DRM30 accepts the standardized 4.5–20 kHz occupancies;
DRM+ and `Auto` use a 100 kHz slice so automatic mode can search both waveform families.

Duplex.description:
What a radio's hardware can do, and whether it can do it at once.

It lives here rather than in the device crate because it is the answer to "what *kind* of
radio is this" that a workspace template filters on and the canvas draws ports from — the
arbitration that uses it ([`sdrmm-device`'s `DuplexState`]) is a separate thing, and stays
with the backends.

channel.description: Logical or absolute channel number named by trunking signalling.

color_code.description:
The mode's network discriminator, under whichever name it publishes: DMR colour code,
NXDN/dPMR RAN or colour code, P25 NAC, YSF has none.

crc_verified.description:
Whether the frame's own CRC matched. `Some(false)` survived only because the channel was
told to ignore the check, so nothing may act on it.

data.description: Decoded packet text, or hexadecimal when its application format is not understood.

destination.description: Numeric destination: talkgroup for a group call, radio ID for a private one.

encrypted.description:
Set when the frame says its payload is encrypted. `Some(false)` is a positive statement
that it is in the clear; `None` means the frame did not say.

errors_corrected.description:
Bit errors the frame's error-correcting codes repaired — the honest signal-quality
readout, since a mode with no audio has no other.

group_call.description: True for a talkgroup call, false for a call addressed to one radio.

message_indicator.description: P25 encryption message indicator as the 72-bit hexadecimal value on the wire.

opcode.description:
Name of the signalling opcode for a control frame — "group voice channel grant",
"preamble", … — as its specification names it.

rest_channel.description: Capacity Plus logical slot number carrying the rest channel.

slot.description: TDMA timeslot, 1 or 2 — DMR only; every other mode here is single-slot.

source.description: Numeric source address — DMR/NXDN/dPMR radio ID, P25 source unit.

source_call.description: Source callsign — the modes that address by callsign rather than by number.

talker_alias.description: DMR talker alias assembled from its header and continuation LCs.

text.description:
Free text the frame carried: a D-Star slow-data message, a YSF radio ID, an M17 meta
field.

oneOf.description:
Set where the signalling names its own flavour, so a follower keys on a discriminant
rather than on the wording of [`DvFrame::opcode`].

via.description: The repeater or reflector the call is routed through: D-Star RPT1/RPT2.

DvFrameKind.description:
What the burst was carrying. Every mode distinguishes these four, whatever it calls them:
the frame that opens a transmission and names the parties, the voice frames that follow,
the one that closes it, and the signalling that travels outside a call.

DvMode.description:
Which digital-voice mode a [`DvFrame`] was heard on ( wave 3). One event type
serves all of them because the *question* is the same in every mode — who is talking, to
whom, on which network — and only the names for it differ.

DvSlotActivity.description: Activity advertised for one DMR timeslot by a Short LC activity update.

DvTrunkProtocol.description:
What the signalling turned out to be. An observation, so it has no "auto" —
[`crate::DmrTrunkProtocol`] is what an operator asks the node for.

ExportFormat.description:
Export format for `GET /api/decoderlog/export/{format}` (: CSV/JSON). It is a
path segment, not a query field: `serde_urlencoded` cannot flatten a struct, so sharing
[`DecoderLogQuery`] across list/export/clear requires the format to live elsewhere.

options.description:
The values the setting accepts, each carrying the driver's own words for it where it
has them: `direct_samp` is written as `0`/`1`/`2` and read as Off/I-ADC/Q-ADC.

ExtraSetting.description:
A typed device-specific setting the client renders generically when it has no
first-class UI (: "typed extra settings").

ExtraValue.description: A value for one [`ExtraSetting`], keyed by its name. `value` is bool/number/string.

FreeDvMode.description:
FreeDV air-interface generation. The initial implementation supports the interoperable
1600 mode; making the generation explicit prevents a future default change from silently
selecting an incompatible waveform on a saved channel.

GainStage.description: A named gain stage with its range in dB (e.g. RTL-SDR tuner gain, HackRF LNA/VGA).

GainValue.description: A gain-stage value in dB, keyed by the stage name from [`GainStage`].

GnssFrame.description: GPS L1 C/A acquisition state or one parity-checked NAV subframe.

GnssParams.description: Educational GPS L1 C/A acquisition and NAV-message settings.

doppler_hz.description: Symmetric acquisition search span around the tuned L1 carrier.

prn.description:
Space-vehicle PRN to acquire. A focused single-PRN view keeps every correlation result
inspectable and bounds the work done on the DSP thread.

threshold.description: Acquisition peak divided by the mean correlation floor.

radial_slope_deg.description:
How far the radials droop below horizontal. Sloping them raises the feedpoint
impedance from about 36 Ω towards 50 Ω.

IdentFeatures.description:
The measurements a classification was made from, carried so the decision can be checked
rather than taken on trust — an operator staring at an unfamiliar signal needs the numbers,
not just the verdict.

carrier_db.description:
The strongest spectral line over the median of the occupied band, in dB — how much of
a carrier there is.

duty.description: Fraction of the observation the carrier was keyed on. 1.0 for a continuous transmission.

envelope_variation.description:
Standard deviation of the envelope over its own mean. Zero for a constant-envelope
mode, large for anything that carries information in amplitude.

frequency_levels.description:
Instantaneous-frequency levels the discriminator resolved: 2 or 4 for keyed modes, 1
for a carrier, 0 when the distribution is a continuum.

frequency_spread_hz.description:
Spread of the instantaneous frequency, in Hz — the deviation of an analog FM signal,
and roughly the outer deviation of a keyed one.

keying_depth_db.description:
Keyed-on level over keyed-off level, in dB — how deep the keying goes, which is what
separates a switched carrier from one that is merely fading.

quartic_line_db.description: The same for the fourth power, which is what QPSK makes.

spectral_asymmetry.description:
Power imbalance about the strongest spectral line, `(upper − lower) / total`. Zero for
a symmetric spectrum (AM, FM, most digital modes), ±1 for a single sideband.

spectral_flatness.description: Wiener entropy of the occupied band: 1.0 is white, 0.0 is a single tone.

square_line_db.description:
Strength of the spectral line the squared signal produces, over its own floor, in dB.
A BPSK signal makes one; so does MSK, which is why the FSK tests run first.

IdentParams.description:
The signal identifier: what to search, how often to answer, and how loud a thing has to be
before it is one.

bandwidth_hz.description:
Slice searched for a signal, in Hz. Wide by default because the point of the mode is to
be pointed at something unknown — narrowing it is what an operator does once they can
see where the thing actually sits.

interval_ms.description:
Milliseconds between reports. Each one analyses the samples since the last, so this is
both the report cadence and the observation the answer stands on — up to a little over a
second, past which the cadence keeps lengthening and each report describes the second
before it rather than the whole gap.

threshold_db.description: How far above the measured noise floor a bin must sit to be part of a signal, in dB.

IdentReport.description:
What the signal identifier made of the slice it was pointed at.

Emitted on a cadence rather than per frame: there is no frame here. Each report describes one
observation window, so a stream of them is a record of what was on the air and when.

center_offset_hz.description:
Where the signal's centre sits relative to the channel's own offset, in Hz — how far
the operator is off tune.

confidence.description: How firmly the classifier held that answer, 0 to 1.

deviation_hz.description: Peak frequency deviation of a keyed or analog FM signal, in Hz.

oneOf.description:
Which sideband, when the modulation is [`Modulation::Ssb`] and the signal sits wholly to
one side of where the channel is tuned.

snr_db.description: Signal-to-noise ratio in the occupied band, in dB.

symbol_rate_hz.description: Symbols per second, when a symbol clock was found.

apex_angle_deg.description: Angle between the two legs. 180° is a flat dipole; the legs shorten as it closes.

LicenseTextResponse.description:
`GET /api/about/licenses/{id}` — one license text, addressed by content.

Texts are addressed by a hash of themselves because that is what deduplicates them: several
hundred crates offer Apache-2.0 and ship byte-identical copies of it, while every MIT copy
differs in its copyright line and none may be collapsed into another. Content addressing
keeps the first case cheap without lying about the second.

Modulation.description:
The modulation family a [`IdentReport`] settled on.

Coarse on purpose. What a receiver can read off an unknown waveform is how its envelope, its
instantaneous frequency and its spectrum behave, and those separate *families* — they do not
separate the variants inside one, which is what the protocol candidates are for.

bandwidth_hz.description: Width of the CW filter around the channel offset, in Hz.

wpm.description: Fixed sending speed in words per minute; `None` tracks the speed from the signal.

MorseText.description: A run of decoded Morse characters plus the speed the tracker settled on.

wpm.description: Estimated sending speed in words per minute (PARIS standard).

NavtexMessage.description:
One NAVTEX broadcast (: SITOR-B over 100 baud FSK). The `ZCZC B1B2B3B4` header is
parsed out because that is what a receiver filters on — station, subject and serial are how
a ship decides whether it has already seen this message.

complete.description:
True when the broadcast ended with `NNNN`; false when the carrier or the phasing was
lost and the partial text was flushed instead.

errors_corrected.description: Characters the mode-B time diversity repaired from the repeat copy.

serial.description: B3B4 — serial number, 00–99, which a receiver uses to suppress repeats.

station.description: B1 — transmitting station within the NAVAREA.

NavtexParams.description:
NAVTEX is a single-purpose broadcast: 100 baud, 170 Hz shift, CCIR 476 (ITU-R M.540), so
there is nothing to tune but the sideband the receiver happens to be on.

invert.description: Swap mark and space (equivalent to reversing the sideband).

node.description: Patch-node identity. A set permits one active exporter and only its owner may stop it.

NetworkExportSettings.description:
An unframed, interleaved IQ stream sent to a network analysis tool.

UDP preserves datagram boundaries but carries no sequence header. TCP is one continuous byte
stream. In both cases the receiver must be configured with the radio's sample rate and center
frequency separately.

overruns.description: Capture-ring samples lost while this export was active.

ctcss_hz.description:
The CTCSS tone to open on, in Hz. One of the 50 standard tones (EIA/TIA-603); anything
else is refused, because the detector only searches those.

dcs_code.description:
The DCS code to open on, as the three octal digits a radio displays — `23` for 023,
`754` for 754. One of the 83 standard codes.

The standard list is not a convenience: the Golay code DCS is built on is cyclic, so
only a set with no rotation aliasing between its members can be read back unambiguously
from a continuously repeating word. A code's *inverse* is another code in the list —
023 received through an inverted discriminator is 047 — so there is no polarity switch
here, and none on a radio either.

NmeaDeviceInfo.description: One serial port the server can currently offer to an NMEA GPS node.

oneOf.description: Spectrum + waterfall over a device's IQ.
Client-side audio mix (: the server ships streams, not a mix).
MapLibre, one layer per connected decoder.
A drive survey of one RF slice, pairing spectrum power with GPS fixes.

data.description: A drive survey of one RF slice, pairing spectrum power with GPS fixes.

oneOf.description:
The live picture a decoder holds — an RDS station, a table of aircraft, a teleprinter
roll — one readout per connected decoder. This is the *state* a decoder accumulates, which
is the half of its output that a log row cannot carry; the frames themselves are read in
[`NodeBody::DecoderLog`], so nothing here repeats it.
The stored decoder log, filtered to the decoders wired into it.
The raster a video channel scans out.
SigMF recording of a device's IQ.
Unframed raw IQ sent over UDP datagrams or a TCP byte stream.

data.description: Unframed raw IQ sent over UDP datagrams or a TCP byte stream.

oneOf.description: CSV/JSON export of the stored decoder log.

NodeTypeInfo.description:
One entry of the node palette the client renders its "add node" menu from (: the client
renders what the server describes).

needs_channel_type.description:
Channel nodes need a type from `GET /api/channeltypes`; the menu offers one entry per
descriptor rather than one entry for "channel".

NoiseBlankerSettings.description: Impulse blanker, applied to the channel's IQ ahead of its selectivity filter.

threshold.description:
How far above the channel's average magnitude a sample has to sit to be cut out, as a
multiple of it. Lower blanks more, and eventually blanks the signal.

NotchSettings.description: One operator-placed notch in the audio.

width_hz.description:
−3 dB width of the null. Narrow removes a heterodyne and leaves the voice; wide takes a
bite out of both.

NxdnBandwidth.description:
The two NXDN channel widths. They are different radios as far as the receiver is
concerned: 6.25 kHz halves both the symbol rate and the deviation of the 12.5 kHz one.

OccupancyBucket.description: One frequency bucket's occupancy statistics ( band-occupancy analytics).

by_hour.description:
Duty per hour of the day, UTC, 24 entries. An hour never observed reads `0.0` — which is
why `samples` matters.

duty.description: Fraction of observations in which this bucket carried a signal, `0.0..=1.0`.

last_seen.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of the most recent observation.

samples.description:
Observations behind that fraction. A duty cycle from three sightings is not a measurement,
and this is what lets a reader tell the difference.

OccupancyReport.description: `GET /api/occupancy` — how much of the time each slice of spectrum has been in use.

since.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of the first observation, or empty before there is one.

PatchApplyReport.description:
`POST /api/workspaces/{id}/apply` — what applying the workspace did.

Apply is additive and idempotent: it opens the radios the graph names and adds the channels it
draws, and never closes or deletes anything. Removing a node is a gesture with its own
endpoint; a reconciler that also deleted would turn "this workspace has fewer nodes" into
"close that operator's radio".

bound.description: Every device node that now has a running device set.

opened.description: Device sets opened by this call.

PatchCatalog.description: `GET /api/patch/catalog` — the node palette and its ports.

PatchEdge.description: A wire: which stream a node consumes, and from whom.

id.description: Client-generated, unique within the graph, stable for the node's life.

label.description: User-renamed caption; `None` renders the kind's default name.

PatchNode.description:
One node: what it is, where it sits, and what the operator called it.

There is no `pinned` flag: rack membership is the single truth for "this face is being
operated", and two representations of one fact drift.

PatchRefusal.description: One node apply could not satisfy.

PlaybackRequest.description:
`POST /api/devicesets/{ds}/playback` — drive the replay transport of a set whose device is
a recording. Looping is not an action here: it is the `loop` device setting, applied like
any other (see [`crate::PlaybackStatus`]).

position_samples.description:
Where [`PlaybackAction::Seek`] should land, in samples from the start; clamped to the
end of the recording. Ignored by every other action, and absent means the start.

PlaybackStatus.description:
Transport of a device set replaying a recording (`virtual:file:`). Absent on a live radio:
there is no position to seek in a signal that is still arriving.

Whether it loops is *not* here — that is `loop` in [`DeviceSettings::extra`], a setting the
radio carries and a workspace saves. Pause and position are the opposite: reopening a patch
must not restore a paused transport, so they live only in this live status.

position_samples.description: Samples replayed from the start of the recording.

total_samples.description:
Samples the recording holds. Read off the data file, so a crash-truncated pair reports
what can actually be replayed rather than what its metadata claims.

PocsagBaud.description:
Bit rate of a POCSAG transmission. Pagers on one frequency may use several, so `Auto`
(the default) locks onto whichever preamble it finds.

baud.description: Bit rate the batch was decoded at.

errors_corrected.description: Single-bit errors the BCH(31,21) decoder repaired across the message's codewords.

invert.description:
Swap mark and space: some transmitters (and some receiver chains) invert the
discriminator polarity, which turns every codeword into noise.

PortCondition.description:
When a port exists. A conditional port depends on what is *behind* the node — the channel type
it names, or the radio it is bound to — and those answers live once in [`ChannelDescriptor`]
and [`Capabilities`]. The catalog states the dependency instead of the client inventing port
names for it.

PortDirection.description: Which side of a node a port sits on.

PortRepeat.description:
How many of a port a node really has. A repeating port is a *family*: the catalog is
per-build static and cannot see how many streams a radio delivers, so it ships the base spec
with this flag and whoever can see the backing expands it — one port per stream, named by
[`stream_port`].

PortSpec.description: One port of a node type.

multi.description:
Whether more than one edge may touch this port. A *stream* output fans out — one device
feeds N channels, scopes and a recorder, which is today's device set drawn — but an
ownership output does not: a scanner drives one radio, because one sweep is what the
engine runs. So arity is stated on both sides and checked on both sides.

name.description: Stable slug, unique within its node and direction; this is what an edge names.

Position.description: Canvas position of a node, in React Flow's coordinate space.

PositionFix.description:
One live station fix. Optional measurements stay absent when the provider did not report
them; latitude and longitude are always a complete, validated pair.

time.description:
RFC3339 UTC. Providers without their own timestamp are stamped when the server receives
the fix.

oneOf.description: The geolocation provider exposed by the desktop WebView.
A gpsd JSON endpoint, normally `127.0.0.1:2947`.

An NMEA 0183 serial device. Receivers push sentences; `update_interval_ms` limits how
often complete fixes are published to live consumers without attempting proprietary
receiver configuration commands.

PresetDevice.description: One device node's radio settings and channels, as the preset captured them.

device_id.description:
`driver:key` of the radio it was captured on. The fallback match, so a preset still lands
after the node was redrawn, and what the client names in the list.

node.description:
[`crate::PatchNode::id`] of the device node this was captured from — the primary match on
apply, and the only one that is right when a patch draws two of the same radio.

devices.description: How many radios the preset carries, denormalized so the list never parses a blob.

ProtocolMatch.description: One protocol the waveform could be, and what says so.

confirmed.description:
Set when the protocol's own framing was found in the signal, not merely resembled. A
confirmed match is an answer; an unconfirmed one is a shortlist entry.

score.description: How well the measurements fit the protocol's signature, 0 to 1.

type_id.description:
The channel type that decodes it, when this build has one — what the client offers to
switch the channel to.

why.description: The evidence, in a phrase: what matched, or what was recognised.

PskParams.description: Receive options shared by the BPSK31 and BPSK63 Varicode channels.

invert.description: Reverse differential bit polarity for an inverted receive chain.

PskText.description: A run of Varicode text decoded from a BPSK31 or BPSK63 carrier.

RackCell.description: One pinned face on the rack grid.

x.description: Whole grid cells from the left / top.

RackSlot.description: One pinned node and the cells it occupies.

RadioClockFrame.description: One complete civil-time minute recovered from a long-wave radio-clock service.

datetime.description:
ISO 8601 civil time carried on air. DCF77, MSF and JJY include their UTC offset;
WWVB is UTC.

invert.description: Reverse the received AM envelope for an inverting receiver or recording.

RadioClockStandard.description: Long-wave civil time service carried by the radio-clock channel.

Range.description: An inclusive numeric range with an optional step, in the setting's native unit.

RdsUpdate.description:
RDS state after a group changed it (: 57 kHz BPSK, group/AF/RT decode). RDS is a
slowly-accreting picture rather than a stream of independent frames, so an event is the
current best view of the station, emitted only when a field actually changed.

alt_freqs_hz.description: Alternative frequencies in Hz, as advertised in group 0A.

block_errors.description: Blocks rejected by the syndrome check since the channel started.

groups.description: Groups accepted since the channel started.

pi.description: Programme Identification, as the 4 hex digits everyone quotes it by.

ps.description: Programme Service name (8 chars), once every segment has been seen.

pty_name.description: Programme Type name for [`RdsUpdate::pty`] under the RDS (EU) table.

radiotext.description: RadioText (up to 64 chars), once the A/B flag closes a message.

RecordRequest.description:
`POST /api/devicesets/{ds}/record` — start or stop recording the set's raw IQ stream
(: the recording path is lossless).

stream.description:
Which receive stream a start records — one recording per set, on a named stream.
Defaults to 0, the only stream a single-stream radio has.

RecordingFormat.description:
Container a recording is downloaded in. A query field rather than a path segment (unlike
[`ExportFormat`]): the format is optional here, and giving a path segment a default would
mean two routes for one resource.

RecordingInfo.description:
One finalized SigMF recording in the library (: the files on disk are the source
of truth; this row is its SQLite index entry).

device_id.description:
`driver:key` that replays this recording (`virtual:file:<stem>`), usable directly
in `POST /api/devicesets`.

device_label.description: Label of the device the recording was captured from (SigMF `core:hw`).

file.description: Recording stem: file name without directory or `.sigmf-*` extension.

RecordingStatus.description:
Live IQ recording on a device set (: the recording path is lossless, so a writer
fault must surface here rather than dropping samples silently).

error.description:
Fatal recording fault (queue overflow, disk error); the writer has stopped but the
cause stays visible (CLAUDE.md no-silent-failure).

file.description: Recording stem: file name without directory or `.sigmf-*` extension.

samples.description: Samples written to the `.sigmf-data` file so far.

stream.description:
Which of the device's receive streams is being recorded. Defaults to 0 because a
status from before multi-stream devices names no stream and means the only one its
radio had.

invert.description: Swap mark and space (equivalent to reversing the sideband).

shift_hz.description: Mark/space separation in Hz (170 amateur, 450/850 commercial).

unshift_on_space.description:
Return to the letters table after a space — the usual amateur convention, which
recovers a stream that lost its shift character.

RttyStopBits.description: RTTY stop-bit length in bit periods. 45.45 baud amateur RTTY uses 1.5.

RttyText.description: A run of decoded RTTY characters (: Baudot over FSK).

ScanRange.description:
One contiguous span to sweep, expanded to `start_hz, start_hz + step_hz, …` up to and
including `stop_hz` when it lands on a step.

oneOf.description: Required for `start`, ignored by `stop`.

ScanSettings.description: What a scan covers and how it behaves on a hit (: "frequency scanner").

dwell_ms.description:
Measurement window per device tuning. Every target inside the tuning's passband is
measured from the same spectrum frames, so this is per *tuning*, not per target.

hold_channel.description:
Channel retuned onto a hit so its audio (or decoder) follows the scan. `None` scans
without listening — the hit log alone.

measure_bw_hz.description: Bandwidth measured around each target; also the width the hold channel is judged over.

ranges.description: Ranges to expand into targets. May be empty if `frequencies` is not.

resume_ms.description: How long a held target must stay below the threshold before the sweep resumes.

threshold_db.description:
A target counts as active when its measured power reaches this level, in dBFS on the
device's spectrum tap.

ScanState.description: What the scanner is doing right now.

ScannerStatus.description:
Live scanner state, projected onto the device set and pushed as
[`crate::ServerEvent::ScannerUpdate`] while a scan runs.

oneOf.description:
What the decoders heard shortly before this client connected, oldest first, sent once
after [`ServerEvent::Hello`].

Decodes are pushed and never replayed, so a reloaded browser used to start with an empty
map and refill it only as contacts happened to transmit again — a gap in the server, since
the engine had been decoding the whole time. The server keeps a bounded, in-memory buffer
of the last few records per station and hands it over on connect.

Raw records rather than merged tracks, on purpose: the client already merges a position
frame onto an earlier identity frame, and replaying what it would have received reaches
the same state through the same code instead of a second implementation of that rule.
Records are aggregated by station id, so an event with no identity is never in here.

SignalMapNode.description: The IQ-relative slice a signal survey measures while pairing spectrum frames with positions.

A single device set changed (settings, status, or its channels).

The stored bookmarks changed; refetch `GET /api/bookmarks`.
The recordings index changed; refetch `GET /api/recordings`.

The number of connected clients changed; refetch `GET /api/clients`. Server-owned
state (connections are not an engine concept), so it travels through `emit_scope`
like presets and bookmarks do.

The stored decoder log changed *structurally* (cleared, pruned). Individual decodes
arrive as [`ServerEvent::Decoded`] and are appended client-side — invalidating per
decode would refetch the whole log hundreds of times a second under ADS-B traffic.

StateScope.description:
Granularity of a `StateChanged` invalidation. The client maps each scope to the
TanStack Query keys it must invalidate (: the *only* cache-invalidation path).

StateSnapshot.description: Full state snapshot for initial load ( `GET /api/state`).

revision.description: Monotonic revision; bumps on every mutation so clients can detect missed events.

StreamKind.description:
Which binary stream a control event refers to. Every id is allocated per connection, from a
range per class, but only the pair `(kind, stream_id)` identifies a stream — events must
carry the kind or a spectrum stop is indistinguishable from an audio one.

StreamScope.description:
Which device settings each receive stream holds on its own, rather than sharing with the rest
of the radio. All-false — the default, and what every capability set from before this field
describes — is the single-stream radio.

Sample rate is deliberately absent and stays shared: one device, one clock domain. Channel
rate validation, the recorder's SigMF `core:sample_rate` and the DSP lanes all assume it.

antenna.description: Each stream selects its own antenna port.

gain.description:
Each stream has its own gain stages. True on nearly every multi-stream radio, including
the coherent arrays: per-channel gain calibration is how an array is levelled.

tuning.description:
Each stream tunes independently. False on a coherent array — the streams share one
tuner reference and tuning them apart is what a coherent array must never do — and true
on a radio with a synthesizer per stream.

StreamSettings.description:
One stream's overrides of the radio-wide [`DeviceSettings`]. Absent fields fall back to the
radio-wide value — [`DeviceSettings::for_stream`] is the one place that resolution lives.

SubghzFrame.description:
One sub-GHz burst: a remote, a sensor, a TPMS. Repeats of the same payload inside a short
window collapse into one frame with a count, because every one of these devices sends its
payload several times and a log with eight identical rows is a worse log.

address.description: EV1527 reading of a 24-bit payload: the 20-bit transmitter address.

bits.description: Decoded payload length in bits; 0 for a raw capture.

button.description: EV1527 reading of a 24-bit payload: the 4 button bits.

data.description: Payload as hex, MSB first, left-padded to whole bytes.

repeats.description: How many times the identical payload arrived inside the collapse window.

short_us.description: The base pulse period the frame was measured against, in µs.

timings_us.description:
Raw pulse/gap durations in µs, pulse first — what a Flipper shows for a signal it
cannot name. Truncated, so this is for inspection, not replay.

tri_state.description: PT2262 reading: 12 tri-state symbols as `0`, `1` and `F`, when every bit pair is one.

bandwidth_hz.description:
Detection bandwidth in Hz. Wide by radio standards on purpose: a SAW-controlled remote
may sit tens of kHz off its nominal 433.92 MHz, and a filter narrow enough to be
"correct" would simply miss it.

frame_gap_us.description:
Silence that ends a frame, in µs. Must exceed the longest gap *inside* a frame — the
PT2262/EV1527 sync gap is ~31 short periods, around 10 ms at a 320 µs clock.

min_pulse_us.description: Shortest keying edge accepted, in µs. Anything briefer is a noise spike, not a symbol.

TemplateInfo.description:
One built-in workspace template (: the template gallery). Read-only and
device-agnostic — unlike a [`PresetSnapshot`] it names no device, so the same entry
applies to whatever hardware is open, provided the device can tune it.

channels.description: Channels the template creates on the target device set.

description.description: One line for the gallery card.

direction.description:
Which direction the radio has to have. Every built-in template receives; the field is
here because "what kind of radio does this need" is the question the picker asks, and a
transmit template must not be offered on a receiver the day one exists.

min_freq_hz.description:
Tuning span the template needs, so the gallery can mark entries the open device
cannot reach instead of failing on apply.

supported_devices.description:
Devices this template can actually run on, as `driver:key` handles — the server's answer,
computed against each probed radio's [`crate::DeviceProfile`], so the gallery offers a
device only when the template fits it.

A radio whose driver reports no profile is *included*: unknown is not the same as
unsuitable, and hiding a device because its backend cannot answer cheaply would make the
picker lie. Empty on the static table; filled in per request.

Always serialized, unlike the other quiet fields: "no attached radio can run this" is a
real answer the gallery has to render, and eliding it would make it arrive as the absence
that means "nobody asked".

ctcss_hz.description: The CTCSS tone present, in Hz.

dcs_code.description: The DCS code present, as the three octal digits a radio displays.

open.description:
Whether audio is passing. Always true unless the channel was told to gate on a tone:
[`crate::NfmToneMode::Detect`] reports what is there without acting on it.

ToolCategory.description: What kind of thing a tool is, so the launcher can group them.

ToolDescriptor.description: One tool the server can run, as advertised by `GET /api/tools`.

id.description: Stable id, and the tag of this tool's [`ToolRequest`] variant.

needs_hardware.description:
Whether running it needs hardware attached. Feature-gated tools are absent from the
list entirely; this marks the ones that are compiled in but may still find nothing.

summary.description: One line, shown under the name in the launcher.

ToolRequest.description:
`POST /api/tools/run` — one call to one tool. The tag is the tool id, so the body names its
own destination and no path parameter can disagree with it.

ToolResponse.description: What a tool answered, tagged with the same id the request carried.

channel.description: The engine channel doing the following; it has no patch node of its own.

TrunkProblem.description:
A grant the follower could not act on — commonly a traffic channel outside the sampled
bandwidth. Carried in state so the operator sees why a busy system produces no calls.

TrunkSystemStatus.description:
What one `dmr_trunk` node is following. Also how the client attributes follower channels,
which have no patch node, to the system that owns them.

revision.description: The revision the client last saw. A mismatch is a `409`, never a silent overwrite.

deemphasis_us.description: De-emphasis time constant in µs (50 in most of the world, 75 in the Americas).

stereo.description:
Recover the 38 kHz stereo difference signal, making the channel's audio two-channel.
A station without a 19 kHz pilot still plays: L and R carry the same mono programme.

WorkspaceHistory.description:
What undo and redo can reach right now.

The history belongs to the workspace, not to a browser: every client works on the same
arrangement, so they share the steps that lead back out of it. Undoing in one window is a
change like any other, and the rest see it.

WorkspaceInfo.description: `GET /api/workspaces` list entry — the projection a switcher needs, without the workspace.

nodes.description:
Node count, denormalized so the switcher can describe a workspace without parsing its
graph.

revision.description:
Bumped on every stored change. An update carrying a stale revision is refused rather than
silently overwriting another client's arrangement.

band_region.description: [`crate::BandRegion::id`], or `None` to follow the server's default for this install.

WorkspaceSnapshot.description:
The stored body of a workspace (: one JSON snapshot per row, like presets — written
atomically, read whole, never queried by inner field).

active.description: The active workspace, or `None` when the last one was deleted.

WsjtMessage.description: One CRC-verified FT8 or FT4 message from a synchronized receive slot.

WsjtParams.description:
Audio passband searched by an FT8 or FT4 decoder after a USB receiver is placed on the
mode's dial frequency.

WsprParams.description: Audio passband searched by WSPR after a USB receiver is placed on the WSPR dial frequency.

WsprSpot.description: One WSPR beacon spot recovered from a two-minute receive slot.

text.description: Familiar WSPRnet tuple, including a hash marker for an unresolved type-3 callsign.

directors.description: Directors in front of the driven element. Zero is a two-element reflector Yagi.

spacing_wavelengths.description: Boom spacing between neighbouring elements, in wavelengths.
